title: AI-generated CSAM trends, 2025 Data & Insights Report
evidence_paraphrase: 491 reports in 2025 versus 193 in 2024; 8,029 criminal AI-generated images/videos in 2025; 82 additional prohibited items. Combined 2024–25 assessments: 15,036.
limitations: Operational findings, not population prevalence; the unit is reports or media items, not unique victims.

title: AI-generated image trends
evidence_paraphrase: 4,586 criminal AI-generated still images among 449,298 criminal images in 2025; 81 additional prohibited still images.
limitations: Assessment and discovery practices affect the numerator and denominator; counts may include repeated subjects.

title: AI-generated video trends
evidence_paraphrase: 3,443 photorealistic criminal AI videos among 63,682 criminal videos in 2025, versus 13 in 2024; 1 additional prohibited video.
limitations: Use the detailed video page: a conflicting figure of 3,343 appears in the executive-summary PDF.

title: More AI-generated abuse images found in first six months of 2026 than all of 2025
evidence_paraphrase: IWF reports that first-half 2026 photorealistic AI-generated still-image findings exceeded full-year 2025.
limitations: Do not infer a precise 2026 count from the qualitative comparison.

title: Executive summary, Annual Data & Insights Report 2025
evidence_paraphrase: 451,210 total reports assessed; 311,610 confirmed as or linked to CSAM. The executive summary warns against interpreting operational findings as global prevalence.
limitations: PDF text and cover inspected. Its page 18 video number conflicts with detailed video reporting; do not silently reconcile.

publisher: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children
title: Generative AI
evidence_paraphrase: More than 158,000 images/videos categorized by staff as AI-generated from Jan 2023 to Dec 2025; providers marked just over 11,000 over that period.
limitations: Public indexed text; counts represent different annotation processes and not a directly measured provider miss rate.

publisher: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children
title: CyberTipline data
evidence_paraphrase: 2025 reports with a generative-AI nexus exceeded 400,000; more than 182,000 involved possession, generation or attempted generation of GAI CSAM.
limitations: Nexus and subset are reporting categories; no direct comparison with IWF items.

title: Releasing Re-LAION-5B
evidence_paraphrase: LAION states that the Dec 2023 Stanford investigation identified links to potentially illegal material; it withdrew the dataset and worked with child-protection organizations on remediation.
limitations: Publisher account; does not establish that all downstream weights contain or reproduce identified material.

title: Content policy
evidence_paraphrase: Policy requires publishers to take appropriate steps to minimize the risk that ML artifacts facilitate child sexual exploitation material; flagged content may be reviewed.
limitations: Policy statement, not independent audit of enforcement.

title: Model cards
evidence_paraphrase: Model cards carry descriptive metadata and documentation accompanying model repositories.
limitations: Publisher disclosures may be incomplete or inaccurate.

title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
evidence_paraphrase: Latent diffusion moves diffusion computation into a learned compressed representation.
limitations: Architecture paper; no misuse prevalence measurement.

title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
evidence_paraphrase: Introduces an improved latent diffusion system and an optional refinement model.
limitations: Publisher evaluation; does not establish safety of community derivatives.

title: FLUX.1 schnell model card
evidence_paraphrase: Publisher reports a 12-billion-parameter rectified-flow transformer and Apache-2.0 licensing for this release.
limitations: Count is publisher-reported model scale, not measured whole pipeline; license applies to this release.

title: Qwen-Image model card
evidence_paraphrase: Public repository identifies Qwen-Image with 20B parameters.
limitations: Publisher metadata; precision, file sums and measured VRAM not independently audited.

title: MOSS-Image official repository
evidence_paraphrase: Repository describes a 5B-parameter DiT backbone for image generation.
limitations: Backbone count only; no independent capability testing.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
evidence_paraphrase: Low-rank trainable updates can adapt frozen pretrained weights with fewer trainable parameters.
limitations: Original paper is about language models; diffusion application is supported by the next source.

title: Diffusers: LoRA
evidence_paraphrase: Diffusers documents LoRA as a parameter-efficient method available in multiple image model families.
limitations: Technical documentation, not an abuse-specific experiment.

title: DreamBooth: Fine Tuning Text-to-Image Diffusion Models for Subject-Driven Generation
evidence_paraphrase: Research demonstrates subject-driven generation using adapted diffusion models.
limitations: Consent and identity risks discussed in this manuscript are analysis, not measured incidence in this paper.

title: Diffusers: Reduce memory usage
evidence_paraphrase: Documentation describes memory-management methods and notes that architecture affects their benefits.
limitations: Actual latency and memory depend on hardware, implementation and workload.

title: Runpod documentation
evidence_paraphrase: Public endpoints and hosted GPU workloads are documented.
limitations: No pricing, moderation efficacy or configuration benchmark was measured.

title: Malicious actors manipulating photos and videos to create explicit content and sextortion schemes
evidence_paraphrase: Public advisory describes reports of manipulated imagery used in sexual extortion and harassment.
limitations: Alert establishes a documented pattern, not global incidence or attribution to particular models.

title: Notice on financially motivated sextortion
evidence_paraphrase: Identifies financially motivated sextortion as a financial-crime concern and describes synthetic imagery in victim reports.
limitations: No payment-channel abuse tutorial or evasion details retained.

title: Recapping our 2022 coordinated inauthentic behavior enforcements
evidence_paraphrase: More than two-thirds of networks disrupted that year featured accounts with likely GAN-generated profile photos.
limitations: Denominator is disrupted networks, not all accounts or all networks.

title: India-based CIB network, H2 2025 indicators
evidence_paraphrase: Publisher reports an India-focused network using AI-generated profile pictures and other generated content.
limitations: Network-specific enforcement report; not proof of nation-wide prevalence.

publisher: Journal of Online Trust and Safety
title: Characteristics and Prevalence of Fake Social Media Profiles with AI-generated Faces
evidence_paraphrase: The study assembled a dataset of 1,420 X/Twitter accounts with GAN-generated profile photos and documented inauthentic uses.
limitations: Selected dataset; not a representative count of platform accounts.

title: OperationFFS: Fake Face Swarm
evidence_paraphrase: Independent investigation documents a coordinated inauthentic network involving synthetic profile faces.
limitations: Case-based evidence; historical GAN results may not transfer to modern diffusion.

title: Our approach to labeling AI-generated content and manipulated media
evidence_paraphrase: Describes AI info labels based on industry signals or self-disclosure.
limitations: Label presence is not a verdict of deception; labels do not cover all media.

title: Understanding how this content was made disclosures
evidence_paraphrase: Describes AI disclosure labels and carrying forward supported C2PA credentials for wholly AI-generated videos.
limitations: Platform documentation; policy and interfaces may change.

title: AI-generated content
evidence_paraphrase: Creators can disclose AI-generated content; users can report prohibited AI impersonation.
limitations: Indexed help text; full enforcement rules were not independently evaluated.

title: Authenticity policy
evidence_paraphrase: Prohibits harmful misleading synthetic/manipulated media and specified inauthentic behavior.
limitations: Context and harm matter; not a blanket prohibition on fictional accounts.

title: Updated advertising guides to combat deceptive reviews and endorsements
evidence_paraphrase: Revised guides clarify that endorsements include virtual influencers and fake reviews; disclosures and truthful endorsements matter.
limitations: US advertising guidance; not universal platform monetization rules.

title: Reducing Risks Posed by Synthetic Content, NIST AI 100-4
evidence_paraphrase: Reviews provenance, watermarking, metadata and detection as complementary transparency techniques.
limitations: Overview does not establish a universally reliable detector.

publisher: Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity
title: Content Credentials technical specification v2.5
evidence_paraphrase: Defines an interoperable manifest and assertion framework for content provenance.
limitations: Signed assertions do not establish real-world factual truth or consent.

title: GenImage: A Million-Scale Benchmark for Detecting AI-Generated Image
evidence_paraphrase: Million-scale benchmark includes diffusion and GAN images with evaluation tasks for generalization.
limitations: Benchmark performance does not imply production accuracy or reliable CSAM classification.

title: DailyBench: A Unified Benchmark for AI-Generated and Manipulated Images from Modern Generative Models
evidence_paraphrase: Proposes evaluation of full synthesis and localized edits across modern generators.
limitations: Preprint; independent replication not checked.

publisher: Government of India, Press Information Bureau
title: Government response on deepfake regulatory framework
evidence_paraphrase: Summarizes IT Act sections 66C, 66D, 66E, 67 and 67A and February 2026 IT Rules amendments for synthetic information.
limitations: Government summary, not case-specific legal advice; read current primary text and commencement provisions.

title: FAQ: IT Rules 2026 amendments
evidence_paraphrase: Explains a dedicated synthetic-generated-information due diligence framework in Rule 3(3).
limitations: Indexed summary only; exact deadlines and exceptions require full legal text.

title: AI Act, Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, Article 50
evidence_paraphrase: Article 50 establishes transparency duties for specified synthetic outputs and deepfakes.
limitations: Exceptions and actor roles matter; disclosure does not legalize prohibited content.

title: Guidelines on transparency obligations
evidence_paraphrase: Commission states Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026.
limitations: Read applicable guidance and national enforcement context.

title: Complying with the TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence_paraphrase: Section 3 enforcement began 19 May 2026; covered platforms have 48 hours from valid requests to remove content and known identical copies.
limitations: Applies to covered platforms and qualifying notices; not all online images or services.

title: Crime and Policing Act 2026: intimate image abuse factsheet
evidence_paraphrase: Explains amendments concerning intimate-image abuse and time-bound takedown duties.
limitations: Enactment and commencement must be distinguished; not all provisions automatically operative.

title: Cybercrime prosecution guidance
evidence_paraphrase: Identifies Sexual Offences Act provisions for purported intimate images and generators.
limitations: Prosecutorial guidance; territorial scope and effective dates require checking.

title: Image-based abuse
evidence_paraphrase: Defines image-based abuse support to include images digitally altered or faked to resemble a person.
limitations: Regulator guidance; not a complete criminal-law analysis.

title: Bill C-16, Protecting Victims Act, Royal Assent
evidence_paraphrase: Enacted text extends the intimate-image offence definition to qualifying realistic synthetic representations.
limitations: Royal assent verified; provision-level effective dates need legal review.

title: Government reply concerning sexual deepfakes
evidence_paraphrase: Government notes possible criminal defamation or insult depending on case facts.
limitations: Not a blanket synthetic-image ban; translation and latest statute check needed.

title: Act on Special Cases Concerning Punishment of Sexual Crimes, Article 14-2
evidence_paraphrase: English statutory text addresses nonconsensual sexual editing or synthesis of a person’s face, body or voice.
limitations: Verify authoritative Korean text, amendments and effective dates for specific cases.

title: PixArt-Sigma official repository
evidence_paraphrase: Publisher describes a diffusion transformer for high-resolution image generation and lists a 0.6B Sigma variant.
limitations: Publisher metadata; no independent size or safety audit.

title: SANA official repository
evidence_paraphrase: Project documents efficient image generation; its README lists a 0.6B SANA variant.
limitations: Publisher benchmarks are not independently replicated.

title: Z-Image-Turbo model card
evidence_paraphrase: Repository metadata identifies a 6B image-generation model family.
limitations: No full-pipeline size, VRAM or safety verification.

title: Lumina-Image 2.0 model card
evidence_paraphrase: Official model card identifies a unified image-generative framework and a Diffusers implementation.
limitations: Parameter count and licensing were not audited.

title: Information Technology Act, 2000
evidence_paraphrase: Official statutory entry for the IT Act.
limitations: Specific elements and applicability to synthetic depictions need legal analysis.

title: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
evidence_paraphrase: Official statutory entry for child protection against sexual offences, including pornography.
limitations: Do not infer that every synthetic depiction meets every statutory element; consult current text and judgments.

title: Deepfake abuse is abuse: Disrupting Harm Phase 2 findings
evidence_paraphrase: Estimated at least 1.2 million internet-using children aged 12–17 across 11 surveyed countries experienced sexual deepfake victimization in one year; estimates weighted by population and internet use.
limitations: Modelled survey estimate, not individual reports, not global prevalence or an open-weight attribution.

title: Through Children’s Eyes: technology-facilitated sexual exploitation and abuse
evidence_paraphrase: Estimated 20 million internet-using children aged 12–17 in 21 countries experienced technology-facilitated sexual exploitation or abuse in a year; nearly 60% of cases involved social platforms; fewer than 1% of experiences reported to authorities. The analysis reports roughly fourfold higher suicidal thoughts/behaviours and self-harm among affected children.
limitations: Broader abuse category, not AI-specific; associations do not establish causation or apply specifically to deepfake victims.

title: Reports from children of fake or manipulated intimate imagery
evidence_paraphrase: 397 suspected-faked reports in 2025 versus 420 in the first half of 2026; actioned reports numbered 221 versus 268.
limitations: Reporter-suspected faking includes AI and other editing; actioned means imagery met legal threshold, not confirmed AI origin or distinct victims.

title: Deepfake Nudes and Young People
evidence_paraphrase: US survey of 1,200 people aged 13–20: approximately 6% of teen respondents reported being targets of deepfake nude creation.
limitations: Self-report survey, not administrative incidence or global estimate; web summary published 2025.

title: The Harms of Image-Based Sexual Abuse
evidence_paraphrase: Qualitative interviews with 75 victim-survivors across the UK, Australia and New Zealand describe enduring disruption across personal and social life.
limitations: Image-based abuse broadly, not exclusively AI; qualitative findings not prevalence or causal estimates.

title: The lived experiences and impacts of sexualized deepfake abuse
evidence_paraphrase: Qualitative interviews with 25 Australian adults, including 15 victim-survivors and 10 perpetrators, report psychological, social and occupational harms, including distress, reputational and relationship damage.
limitations: Abstract-level review; small qualitative sample, not representative and not a child study.

title: Hilliard man sentenced for AI alteration of real minors’ images
evidence_paraphrase: Federal sentence of 14 years for two child pornography crimes; defendant admitted AI alteration of images of real children and distribution of abuse material.
limitations: Multiple offences; cannot isolate AI contribution to sentence; model not attributed.

title: Columbus man sentenced for cyberstalking and AI-generated obscene material
evidence_paraphrase: 15-year federal sentence following guilty pleas for cyberstalking, obscene child sexual abuse representations and publication of digital forgeries.
limitations: Multiple offences, case-specific adjudication; not evidence of general prevalence or model family.

title: Crime and Policing Act 2026: explanatory notes
evidence_paraphrase: Sections 72 and 99 address child sexual abuse image-generators and purported intimate image generators; section 99 includes making, adapting and supplying, with defined defences and intermediary exemptions.
limitations: Enacted text and explanatory notes; commencement, territorial extent and exact elements require verification before legal reliance.

title: FTC Begins Enforcing the TAKE IT DOWN Act
evidence_paraphrase: Section 3 enforcement began 19 May 2026; covered platforms must remove qualifying intimate depictions and known identical copies within 48 hours of a valid request.
limitations: US statutory scope only; does not prove compliance or elimination of all copies.

publisher: US National Telecommunications and Information Administration
title: Dual-Use Foundation Models with Widely Available Model Weights
evidence_paraphrase: Recommended monitoring rather than immediate broad weight restrictions given then-insufficient marginal-risk evidence; preserves future targeted restriction option.
limitations: Historical policy assessment, not current law; scope includes a parameter threshold that can omit image models; no claim that all releases are safe.

title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal: FAQ
evidence_paraphrase: Official reporting portal offers a category for crimes relating to women and children.
limitations: Reporting channel, not evidence of case outcomes or an emergency service.
